execution: Four independent session subagents with fork_turns=none; source instructions supplied by directory, not a native installed-client discovery run. Three actors completed eight specialist planning/assessment cases; one actor completed a generic-workflow-only fallback case.
grading: Author assessment against criteria frozen before actor dispatch; actors did not receive criteria, intended answers or prior outputs. No statistical or causal improvement claim.
model: Inherited session model/settings; no model override.
input_record: inputs-and-criteria.json contains the frozen scenario facts and grading criteria; actor task messages condensed wording and included scoped read/write instructions. Exact orchestration messages remain in the originating session.
artifact_processing: Actor outputs preserved with only the local source-root prefix normalized to repository-relative plugins/. No source/criteria repair was made after these observations.
limits: One planning/assessment observation per case; no complete workflow or application-generation rerun.
No runtime, database, browser UI, provider, native client, billing, deployment or live integration behavior established.
No comparative baseline for the specialist cases; absent-specialist case is a different task, not causal evidence.
Sources explicitly exposed to actors; automatic selection/discovery and installed-client controls were not tested.
Only governance actor consulted external official sources; other actors reported local guidance and supplied scenario facts only.

results.section: 1. Invitations and access changes in the Django application

criteria.criterion: Preserves accepted Django identity choices and separates optional enterprise federation decisions from ordinary invitation design.
criteria.observation: Retains django-allauth/Redis and treats enterprise SSO as an uncommitted customer request.

criteria.criterion: Distinguishes verified identity, organization membership, resource authorization and commercial/billing authority.
criteria.observation: Separates session identity, scoped memberships, resource permissions and finance authority.

criteria.criterion: Defines recipient/grant authority and lifecycle/revocation effects across existing sessions and background work.
criteria.observation: Defines invitation recipient/grant checks and current-authority checks through export publication/download and session/cache changes.

criteria.criterion: Provides meaningful allowed/denied and lifecycle verification without claiming execution or provisioning a provider.
criteria.observation: Plans allowed/denied, concurrent and lifecycle checks and explicitly reports them unexecuted.

criteria.criterion: Derives hierarchy from operational tasks and distinguishes customer operations from finance administration.
criteria.observation: Prioritizes stalled-export/follow-up queues and separates finance administration.

criteria.criterion: Defines organization/time context and meaningful metric freshness/missing/empty semantics.
criteria.observation: Keeps organization/period visible and distinguishes current operational state from delayed analytics, unavailable and zero values.

criteria.criterion: Handles table/filter/selection and important pending/failure/permission states with realistic content and accessible/responsive behavior.
criteria.observation: Defines filtering/pagination, selection scope, organization switching, meaningful states and accessible/responsive checks.

criteria.criterion: Preserves accepted visual direction and separates interface evidence from server authorization or persisted-function claims.
criteria.observation: Preserves established visual components and distinguishes server enforcement and unperformed rendered/usability checks.

criteria.criterion: Separates authenticated event receipt, durable progress, completed entitlement effects and external notification outcomes.
criteria.observation: Separates durable receipt/progress, entitlement effects and notification outcomes.

criteria.criterion: Addresses duplicate/out-of-order delivery and interrupted/ambiguous effects with suitable atomicity/idempotency/reconciliation.
criteria.observation: Proposes inbox/local transaction/outbox/reconciliation using existing processing, including crash and ambiguous email handling.

criteria.criterion: Identifies unresolved customer policy for cancellation/reactivation without inventing accepted grace/data-loss behavior.
criteria.observation: Identifies cancellation timing, entitlement convergence and ambiguous resend decisions as unresolved.

criteria.criterion: Defines relevant failure/restart verification while preserving scope and existing infrastructure.
criteria.observation: Plans interruptions, replay/order and persisted-state verification with no provider action.

criteria.criterion: Assesses territorial applicability and processing roles from actual activities rather than region, nationality or a single universal SaaS role.
criteria.observation: Analyzes operation-specific Article 3 scope and separate controller/processor roles; rejects EU-region readiness inference.

criteria.criterion: Traces relevant provider/support, purpose, retention and rights consequences without defaulting all processing to consent.
criteria.observation: Maps actual support/AI flows, purposes, rights/retention and transfer questions without universal consent.

criteria.criterion: Connects applicable concerns to system/control decisions, evidence gaps and specific unresolved interpretation or customer choices.
criteria.observation: Connects facts to decisions, proposed owners and synthetic verification evidence; unresolved interpretations remain explicit.

criteria.criterion: Uses appropriate official sources and avoids copied-regulation checklists, certification claims or invented implemented controls.
criteria.observation: Consults official sources, notes unavailable restricted materials and avoids a compliance conclusion.

criteria.criterion: Separates new control design/implementation from historical operating evidence and does not backdate or fabricate activity.
criteria.observation: Rejects the unsupported three-month claim and distinguishes a reminder/configuration from performed reviews.

criteria.criterion: Distinguishes relevant report scope and point-in-time versus period evidence without guaranteeing an audit outcome.
criteria.observation: Explains Type 1/Type 2 and readiness options without promising timing/opinion or inventing historical operation.

criteria.criterion: Assesses service boundaries, provider/shared responsibilities and applicable commitments rather than inheriting the cloud provider's assurance.
criteria.observation: Scopes actual service/shared responsibilities and treats provider report as dependency evidence.

criteria.criterion: Prioritizes evidence gaps and real management/auditor decisions without imposing every category or a compliance platform.
criteria.observation: Prioritizes real evidence populations and assurance-owner decisions without compulsory categories/platform.

results.section: 1. PostgreSQL report, pool pressure and tenant context

criteria.criterion: Treats plans, selectivity, pool wait and workload/resource budgets as hypotheses/evidence rather than assuming scans or missing indexes are defects.
criteria.observation: Treats a 60% scan as potentially appropriate and distinguishes estimated plan costs from pool/request time.

criteria.criterion: Accounts for index/write/maintenance and connection/memory tradeoffs with representative before/after verification needs.
criteria.observation: Accounts for index write/storage costs and complete connection/resource budgets; proposes representative comparisons.

criteria.criterion: Recognizes tenant identity trust and pooled-session lifetime/reset boundaries rather than treating a session variable or enabled RLS as complete authority.
criteria.observation: Examines session-variable trust, role/RLS bypass and pool lifetime/reset without assuming isolation.

criteria.criterion: Respects unavailable execution and EXPLAIN ANALYZE effects; does not claim measurement, live mutation or substitute-engine verification.
criteria.observation: Runs no query; explicitly notes unavailable target and executing EXPLAIN/function effects.

results.section: 2. TypeScript utility library packaging and browser support

criteria.criterion: Separates type checking, transpilation, host resolution, runtime globals and emitted/distributed artifacts.
criteria.observation: Separates checking, transpilation, resolution, declarations and runtime APIs.

criteria.criterion: Addresses alias/exports and browser/runtime compatibility against actual promised consumers rather than adopting React or a universal tsconfig.
criteria.observation: Preserves bundler/library scope and addresses alias/export/browser promises without React or universal configuration.

criteria.criterion: Requires meaningful packed external-consumer and public-type/runtime evidence, not just workspace success.
criteria.observation: Requires packed external-consumer public-type/runtime and actual browser evidence.

criteria.criterion: Reports unexecuted checks and preserves the scoped plan-only request and existing tools.
criteria.observation: Keeps repair as a plan and makes all proposed checks unexecuted.

criteria.criterion: Establishes ownership, bounded work, cancellation/completion and blocking communication behavior rather than detaching work by default.
criteria.observation: Defines owned cancellation-aware work, completion and bounded background behavior instead of blanket WithoutCancel.

criteria.criterion: Accounts for a usable shutdown deadline plus separate worker/hijacked-connection lifecycle and accepted-work recovery.
criteria.observation: Uses independent drain budget and accounts for workers, hijacked/WebSocket connections and accepted-work recovery.

criteria.criterion: Distinguishes dynamic race detection from leak/deadlock/logical-race/lifecycle evidence and makes no unsupported success claim.
criteria.observation: Explains race detector limits and proposes leak/blocking/lifecycle tests without claiming success.

criteria.criterion: Preserves version/framework/layout and selects verification for the actual contract without mandatory tooling or coverage targets.
criteria.observation: Preserves framework/layout/version and installs no toolchain or service.

results.section: Proposed behavior and boundaries; verification; guidance read

criteria.criterion: Retains authority, tenant ownership, lifecycle/retention and actual verification outcomes without requiring unavailable specialists.
criteria.observation: Retains resource/tenant authority, membership-change handling, seven-day expiry and cleanup/recovery reasoning.

criteria.criterion: Preserves Ruby/PostgreSQL and existing conventions rather than selecting an installed/preferred stack.
criteria.observation: Preserves Ruby/PostgreSQL and explicitly avoids inferring Rails, a queue or storage provider.

criteria.criterion: Distinguishes missing guidance from missing execution targets and completes useful planning with truthful evidence limits.
criteria.observation: Completes useful planning while distinguishing absent guidance from unavailable execution.

criteria.criterion: Does not expand into implementation, installation, live mutation or repeated requests about settled retention/authority rules.
criteria.observation: Makes no edits/installation/live claims and preserves the accepted seven-day duration while identifying unsettled anchor/semantics.
